items.title: Abuse Case
items.summary: Threat modeling where the LLM can't invent a CVE, and code computes the risk score By Daniel Nweke Project page: https://towardsdatascience.com/abuse-case/ ShipAI is a Towards Data Science project. Watch all the videos here: https://towardsdatascience.com/videos/ Key takeaways. 1. Describe an architecture and GPT-4o builds the system model, data flow diagram, STRIDE threats and business logic abuse scenarios. 2. A second critic pass audits STRIDE category balance, and CWE or ATT&CK IDs missing from offline JSON catalogs are dropped. 3. CVEs come only from the National Vulnerability Database, and the risk score is calculated in TypeScript, not by the LLM. Chapters: 0:00 Why threat modeling stalls 1:01 Beyond STRIDE 3:00 Architecture to data flow diagram 5:54 STRIDE threats 7:33 Business logic abuse 8:53 Live CVEs from NVD 10:03 The risk register 11:15 How it's built

ShipAI is a Towards Data Science project. Watch all the videos here: https://towardsdatascience.com/videos/

items.title: Will today’s kids stop thinking because of AI?
items.summary: Stephen Wolfram points out that there’s now a generation for whom any question can be typed into a phone, and some combination of AI and web search gives them an answer, as if all of human knowledge were askable. He compares it with his own childhood: no cell phones, no way to find someone who didn’t show up at three o’clock. So will that lead to nobody thinking about anything, because they just type it into their AI and it tells them what to do? “Maybe I’m an optimist,” he says, but he thinks the level of what people try to do will go up, while more and more gets automated underneath. From Stephen Wolfram’s livestream “Science & Technology for Kids (and Others)”, October 9, 2026. Full livestream: https://youtube.com/live/YRFfP1YDoVA #Shorts #AI #StephenWolfram #Education #Kids #Technology

items.title: AI Latent Reasoning:  Sep-Latent Token Compression
items.summary: By applying a progressive Attention-Decay mask that selectively starves intermediate reasoning tokens of attention during training, Sep-Latent forces the transformer to compress multi-step logical states into structural separator anchors, and aligns these compressed states with an MLP-projected continuous latent stream via all-layer Euclidean self-distillation. Paired with a dynamic LM-head exit gate that autonomously terminates silent computation based on query complexity, Sep-Latent keeps latent vectors grounded on the vocabulary manifold, cuts training GPU memory by over 50%, and achieves 56.8% accuracy on GSM8k-Aug using an average of just 5.4 tokens; outperforming both explicit CoT (at nearly 5× token compression) and state-of-the-art implicit baselines in accuracy, speed, and symbolic robustness. All rights w/ authors: Sep-Latent: Separator Tokens as Natural Compression Anchors for Implicit Reasoning Yinlong Xu1,2, Jianfeng Huang2, Zhengdong Zhou2, Mingjie Lin2 Fuyu Lv2, Dan Ou2, Hongxia Xu1*, Jian Wu1* from 1 College of Computer Science and Technology, Zhejiang University, Hangzhou, China 2 Alibaba Group, Hangzhou, China arXiv:2610.22924 #aiexplained #discoverai #airesearch

items.title: What Survives When AI Can Build Anything? (with Dr. Richard Socher)
items.summary: #aiforscience #superintelligence #agenticai In Episode #1037, Dr. Richard Socher (CEO and Co-Founder of Recursive) joins @JonKrohnLearns to make the case for automating the scientific method itself. Richard’s startup came out of stealth this year with over half a billion dollars raised to build recursively self-improving superintelligence, and his new book, The Eureka Machine, is already a national bestseller. He also co-founded You.com and the venture firm AIX Ventures, was chief scientist at Salesforce, taught the first university course anywhere on neural networks for NLP, and helped build the ImageNet dataset. In this episode, he traces how AI keeps replacing hand-crafted expertise with scale, lays out the four pillars of his Eureka Machine, argues that hallucinations can be a feature for science, explains why recursive self-improvement within a year or two still rules out an overnight takeoff, and names the software and jobs he expects to endure. items.title: Extract data from MRI reports privately with Sparrow
items.summary: Many organizations won't send medical reports to a public cloud API, yet the results still get retyped by hand. In this video, Sparrow turns an MRI lumbar spine report into structured data: disc levels with grades, measurements as numbers, and the full impression. Sparrow is open source and runs on infrastructure you control, on your own machines or a private cloud GPU, so patient data stays inside your environment. This video uses the online version with a synthetic report. Try it online: https://sparrow.katanaml.io Sparrow on GitHub: https://github.com/katanaml/sparrow Want this on your documents? We set it up on your infrastructure and run a pilot: https://katanaml.io/consulting.html More industry videos: https://www.youtube.com/playlist?list=PLMhQwmybML_A Chapters: 0:00 The problem and why it stays private 2:30 Running the extraction 2:45 The result Sample document: synthetic MRI report created for this video. All names and values are fictional. #Sparrow #OpenSource #MedicalReports

items.title: 🔴 LIVE: Vizag Data Center Hub Shifts to Air-Cooling to Safeguard Water Resources | Front Page

AdaniConneX and Google’s planned $15 billion, 1-gigabyte data center campuses in Visakhapatnam will utilize advanced air-cooling technology instead of conventional water-based evaporative cooling towers, preserving local drinking water and minimizing environmental impact on the Mudasarlova Reservoir. In space technology, ISRO successfully conducted the first ignition test of the full-scale gas generator for its 1,100-kilonewton LME1100 methane engine, advancing India's Next Generation Launch Vehicle (NGLV) and future crewed lunar landing plans. Internationally, Anthropic co-founder Jack Clark highlighted an internal scenario projecting a $44 trillion US economy by 2030, China proposed export controls covering 23 AI technologies, Anthropic launched a Public Benefit Fund, NVIDIA expanded its Nemotron line to run locally on RTX systems while urging suppliers toward TSMC base dies, and Meta released open-weights for Muse Spark Open. Domestically, CERT-In issued an alert regarding AI research agents breaching Indian networks, and India faced capacity utilization challenges amidst its 233 GW solar manufacturing expansion.
